why: The verse names Zechariah among the ra'shim (chief men) Ezra sent for at Ahava, which is B; A is the Parosh descendant of 8:3, and its claim that he was a Levite contradicts the text, since Ezra sent for these men because he had found no Levites.
'Of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom' names the priestly house founded by Aaron's grandson Phinehas, not the contemporary father of Eleazar of 8:33.
Eleazar ben Phinehas weighing the treasure in Ezra's day is the son of a contemporary Phinehas, which is B, not the high priest of Numbers.
Both records are the family head Shephatiah whose descendant Zebadiah ben Michael went up with Ezra, with the same ancestor-of link.
Both records are Timna the sister of Lotan; A states that it is this verse's sister of Lotan, so the woman is held twice.
'Ehud ben Gera, the Benjamite' names Ehud's father, which is A; B is Shimei's father.
Pashhur ben Immer the priest names Pashhur's father (or ancestor), which is B; nothing in the text ties him to A's line through Meshillemith.
Elasah ben Shaphan names Elasah's father, which is B; the text does not say he is Josiah's scribe, and A's family lists no Elasah.
Zedekiah ben Hananiah, a prince in Jehoiakim's court, names Zedekiah's father, which is B, not the prophet son of Azzur.
Both records are Amos, son of Naum and father of Mattathias, at the same place in Luke's genealogy.
'Matthan begat Jacob' names Matthan's son, Joseph's father, which is A, not the patriarch.
'Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary' is Matthan's son, which is A, not the patriarch.
The Levite list names Shebaniah twice (10:10 and 10:12), and B is defined as the second, distinct one at 10:12; A's claim on 10:12 is the conflation B separates.

Elam among the 'chiefs of the people' is the house of Elam (Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu... follow Ezra 2), and A already records him as named on the sealed document at 10:14, so B duplicates him.
'Ater, Hizkijah' echoes 'Ater of Hezekiah' (Ezra 2:16), so the sealer is the house of Ater, which A records; B is the same house held again.
A's notes already place Zadok on the sealed document at 10:21, and B is that same sealer with nothing added.
A's notes already place Rehum on the sealed document at 10:25, and B is that same sealer with nothing added.
A's notes already place Baanah on the sealed document at 10:27, and B is that same sealer with nothing added.
A, the house of Harim of Ezra 2:32, is already noted as sealing at 10:27, and B is that same lay sealer.
A's notes already place Malluch on the sealed document at 10:27, and B is that same lay sealer with nothing added.
NEH 10:2-8 lists priests ('these were the priests', 10:8), so this Hattush is A, the Aaronic priest, not B, David's descendant of the tribe of Judah.
A, the priestly house of Harim, is already noted as sealing at 10:5, and B is that same priestly sealer.
A is the Kadmiel of Nehemiah's day, noted as sealing at 10:9; B is the Levite house-founder of Zerubbabel's return, about a century earlier.
Both records are Hashabiah, son of Bunni and father of Azrikam, in Shemaiah's Levitical pedigree; A adds an unsupported tie to Jeduthun.
Both records are Akkub the gatekeeper named with Talmon after the return.
'Judah ben Hassenuah' names Judah's father, which is A; B is Hodaviah's father in 1CH 9:7.
This Ezra is a priest who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua, generations before Ezra the scribe, so he is B.
Both records are the priest Jeremiah who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua and was ancestor of Hananiah (12:12), with the same family links.
Both records are the priestly house of Jeremiah headed by Hananiah under Joiakim, with the same links.
'Of Ezra, Meshullam' is the priestly house of the Ezra who came up with Zerubbabel (12:1), which is B, not the scribe.
Both records are Meshullam, head of the house of Ezra under Joiakim at 12:13; they differ only in which Ezra they link to.
Both records are the priestly house of Iddo from Zerubbabel's return, which Zechariah headed under Joiakim, and A's notes cite 12:16 itself.
Both records are Shemaiah, ancestor of Jehonathan in the list of priestly houses.
The list is of priests and Levites with Zerubbabel, so Hattush is the priest (A), not David's descendant of the tribe of Judah who went up with Ezra (B).
Both records are the priest Malluch whose house (Melicu/Malluchi) Jonathan headed, which A records through ancestor-of jonathan-11.
Two Jedaiahs stand in the Zerubbabel list (12:6, 12:7); 'of Jedaiah, Nethaneel' follows Hilkiah, so it is the second one, which is B, while A is the son of Joiarib (the first).
Johanan ben Eliashib continues the high-priestly succession of 12:22 (Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, Jaddua), so this is the high priest B.
Both records are Akkub the gatekeeper named with Talmon; A already cites NEH 12:25.
This Meremoth is a priest who came up with Zerubbabel, about eighty years before Meremoth ben Uriah of Ezra's day (A).
Ezra the scribe is named separately at the head of this company (12:36), so the Ezra in this list is a different man, B.
Judah in the dedication procession under Nehemiah is B; A is a Levite of Zerubbabel's return, a century earlier.
B is the Shemaiah of the dedication procession; A is the house-founder ancestor of Jehonathan, and the text does not identify the two.
Both records are Mattaniah ben Micaiah, father of Shemaiah, at the same point of the Asaphite pedigree in 12:35.
Both records are Shemaiah ben Mattaniah, father of Jonathan, at the same point of the pedigree in 12:35.
'His brethren, Shemaiah...' are Zechariah's fellow musicians with David's instruments, which is B, not the priestly house-founder A.
Both records are the priest Iddo who came up with Zerubbabel; A's notes cite NEH 12:1-4, and B's house is the same Iddo's.
Miniamin, a priest with a trumpet at the dedication, is exactly A; B is the house of Miniamin in the Joiakim list (12:17).
Elam among the priests and singers at the dedication is B, not the lay house of Elam from Ezra 2:7.
Jehohanan among the priests and singers at the dedication is B; the text does not make him the head of Amariah's house under Joiakim.
Uzzi among the priests and singers at the dedication is B; the text does not make him the head of Jedaiah's house under Joiakim.
Maadiah in the list of priests with Zerubbabel is the house head B; A is the Maaziah who sealed in Nehemiah's day (10:8), and A's record does not claim this verse.
Both records are the priest Shemaiah, ancestor of Jehonathan (12:18), whose house stands in the Zerubbabel list.
Jeshua, Binnui and Kadmiel as Levites with Zerubbabel are the house of Ezra 2:40, which is A; B is the Levite of Nehemiah's day.
Both records are Zaccur, son of Mattaniah and father of Hanan the treasurer, with identical family links.
Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, is exactly A; B is the Merarite Levite who joined Ezra.
Shemaiah ben Shecaniah, keeper of the east gate and a repairer of the wall, is A; the text does not make him the Davidic Shemaiah of 1CH 3:22 (B).
Both records are Hananiah ben Shelemiah, who repaired the wall, with the same father link.
Both records hold Arah as the father of Shecaniah, Tobiah's father-in-law; B adds the house of Arah from Ezra 2:5.
Both records are the ancestor of the 1,254 'children of Elam' in the return list (EZR 2:7 = NEH 7:12).
Both records are the priestly house of Jedaiah 'of the house of Jeshua' in the return list; A already cites NEH 7:39.
'The children of Jeshua, of Kadmiel' in the return list is the Levite house of Ezra 2:40, which is A; B is the Levite of Nehemiah's day.
A is exactly the Malchijah at Ezra's left hand; B merges him with the sealer and the dedication singer, an identification the text does not make.
Both records are Meshullam standing at Ezra's left hand at the reading of the law, with nothing else to tell them apart.
The Kadmiel on the Levites' stairs in Nehemiah's day is A by definition; B is the house-founder of Zerubbabel's return.
The Kadmiel who called Israel to bless the LORD is A by definition; B is the house-founder of Zerubbabel's return.
'The family of the house of Nathan' is a mourning clan beside the house of David, matching B's house head; nothing points to Nathan the prophet (A).
